title: What is Avalonia
sub: One C# and XAML UI for every system
cards/0/body:
Avalonia is a framework for apps with windows, buttons and lists. Write it once in C# and XAML, and run it on Windows, macOS and Linux, plus iOS, Android and the browser.

It is open source under the MIT license.
cards/1/body:
Usually a button in an app is an operating system button. Avalonia works differently: it draws every pixel itself with the Skia graphics library, like a game engine.

That is why an app looks the same everywhere, and supporting a new platform comes down to "learn to open a window and draw in it".
cards/2/q: Why does an Avalonia app look the same on Windows and macOS?
cards/2/options/0: Avalonia draws every element itself with Skia instead of using system buttons
cards/2/options/1: It copies the Windows style onto the Mac
cards/2/explain: Custom rendering is the core idea behind Avalonia.
cards/3/body:
WPF: Microsoft's XAML framework, Windows only. Avalonia is similar in many ways, and WPF experience carries over.
WinForms: the old forms, Windows only.
.NET MAUI: also cross-platform, but builds the UI from each system's native controls.
cards/4/q: Match each framework to its key trait
cards/5/q: Where can an Avalonia app run? Select all that apply.
cards/5/explain: Plus iOS, Android and embedded Linux with no windowing system.
cards/6/q: You know WPF. What will feel familiar in Avalonia?
cards/6/options/0: XAML, bindings, styles, MVVM: same ideas, different details
cards/6/explain: There are differences too: a different selector-based style system and different names for some properties. We will cover them along the way.
cards/7/body: The look is not fully native: a button on a Mac looks like an Avalonia button, not a macOS one. For many apps, such as editors, tools and CAD, that is actually a plus: every user gets the same interface.
cards/7/deep: For porting large WPF apps there is the commercial Avalonia XPF. It runs almost unchanged WPF code on macOS and Linux.
cards/8/q: How does MAUI differ from Avalonia?
cards/8/options/0: MAUI turns elements into the system's native controls, Avalonia draws them itself
cards/8/explain: Hence the trade-off: MAUI looks native, Avalonia looks the same everywhere.
